transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-02
Start: 15:31 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (Stratos Procurement), Diego Ramirez (Stratos Security), Priya Singh (Stratos Finance)
Links shared: onboarding-deck.pdf (link: https://redwood.docs/stratos/onboarding-deck), pricing-spreadsheet.xlsx (link: https://redwood.docs/stratos/pricing), MSA-redlines (link: https://redwood.docs/stratos/msa-redline)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Alright folks, thanks for joining. quick note on agenda - we wanna run through the MSA redlines, DPA points you flagged, high level SLA expectations, and then pricing/fee routing so procurement knows the approvals. anything else to add?
[00:18] Anya (Stratos): No that's perfect. we also want to capture the cert checklist so we can slot you into our vendor queue. timing is kinda tight — we have a board review mid-July so need clarity.
[00:30] Liam (Redwood SE): Hi all, Liam here. i'll focus on the technical bits — KMS, VPC/private deployment, and some latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:40] Priya (Stratos): quick heads up from finance, we need committed usage numbers and an example fee routing plan — e.g., how billing will be handled if we go dedicated vs hosted.
[00:52] Maya: great. starting with MSA redlines — we received your doc last week. high level, the commercial terms are straightforward but we saw three legal exceptions: indemnity cap, audit window, and data residency clause in the DPA. would you like us to walk through our position on each?
[01:10] Anya: yes please. indemnity cap — our counsel wants a mutual cap at 1x ARR for critical data exposures. I'm assuming Redwood standard is limited to direct damages?
[01:24] Maya: right. our standard limits liability to direct damages up to the greater of $1M or the fees paid in the prior 12 months. can propose a middle ground — 1x ARR if you have high sensitivity, but that usually requires an enterprise T&Cs amendment and sign-off.
[01:40] Diego: also, on audit rights — we can't allow a vendor to run, like, unrestricted penetration tests against prod without a scope. we need a scheduled window and read-only access for compliance.
[01:53] Liam: totally, we can agree to a scoped audit approach. Redwood also offers SOC 2 reports and can facilitate redacted logs. for pen tests we prefer coordinating through our security team and a staging endpoint when possible.
[02:10] Anya: works for us, staging endpoint is acceptable.
[02:18] Priya: on data residency, in the DPA you had a clause that allows cross-border processing for backups. we need backups to remain in EU for EU-origin data.
[02:30] Liam: yes — we have region-aware hosting options. Hosted API by default replicates for durability but for strict EU residency we can enable a EU-only residency profile or recommend Redwood Private (VPC) where data never crosses regions. small caveat: some features like cross-region fallback would be disabled.
[02:53] Diego: and KMS? we need customer-managed keys. Our security policy mandates keys that we can revoke. is BYOK supported?
[03:04] Maya: short answer yes — we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and for dedicated pools with an HSM-backed option. for hosted API, BYOK is available via our HSM/KMS integrations but has an onboarding lead time.
[03:20] Liam: add-on: if you choose customer-managed keys, you lose some of our caching/kv features because we can't persist decrypted cache outside your control — there is a performance hit but it's usually modest.
[03:36] Priya: ok that's important for the pricing model because if caching is limited we expect higher token fees. can you quantify?
[03:45] Liam: rough ballpark — without prefix caching you might see 10–25% increase in token compute for chat workloads depending on hit rate. we can run a short benchmark on your sample prompts.
[03:58] Anya: benchmark would be helpful. next — SLA. What are the SLOs you normally offer?
[04:05] Maya: we publish 99.9% for hosted and can commit to 99.95% for Dedicated with a reserved-capacity contract. credits vary — we issue service credits calculated over monthly measurement windows.
[04:20] Priya: how are credits computed? calendar month? rolling 30? and what is the payout mechanism — invoice credit or cash?
[04:29] Liam: generally calendar month. credits are a percentage of monthly fees for the affected service. typically invoice credit; cash payouts are rare and require legal approval.
[04:39] Diego: we need the measurement windows documented explicitly in the MSA/SLA section — and excluded maintenance windows.
[04:47] Maya: absolutely. we'll provide a draft SLA appendix with exact measurement and maintenance definitions.
[04:53] [05:00] Maya: switching to pricing — Priya, you said you want committed usage options and fee routing?
[05:05] Priya: yes. our procurement team prefers a routing where base access is covered under a platform fee (to be paid by central cloud budget) and overages billed to product teams. also want an idea of discounts for 12/24 month commits.
[05:20] Maya: we can do tiered discounts: 10% off list at 12 months commit, 18% at 24 months, plus a custom reserved capacity price for Dedicated. We'll share a pricing spreadsheet with scenarios.
[05:33] Priya: and approvals — who signs off? If we exceed headcount or spend thresholds we need CFO sign-off. I'll confirm internal thresholds and share them.
[05:40] Anya: timeline — if we want board review mid-July, what's the fastest path?
[05:46] Maya: quickest is we send a clean redline and a commercial term sheet this week, you route internally, then follow-up with legal/infosec deep-dive next week. that would give you something for the board.
[05:58] Diego: deep-dive we want specifics: SOC2 scope, encryption at rest details, key rotation, ingress/egress diagrams, and the incident response SLAs.
[06:11] Liam: we will prepare a security packet — SOC2, architecture diagram, keying options, and a proposed incident response timeline. note: incident response for the platform follows our standard where P1 gets a 1-hour acknowledgement and a rollback/fallback playbook; we can include escalation contacts.
[06:30] Anya: good. one thing on the DPA — there are a couple of clauses about subcontractors. we need a list of subprocessors and the ability to be notified of changes.
[06:42] Maya: standard practice — we publish a subprocessors list and provide a notice period for changes. we can put a 30-day notice in the DPA if needed.
[06:50] Priya: can you confirm data deletion and egress? we need a contractual guarantee of data purge within X days on termination and a simple export path.
[06:59] Liam: yes, data purge within 30 days for most hosted scenarios; for Dedicated we can do same-day purge upon request though there are cert steps. export — we support bulk export via secure S3 paths. we'll document formats and TTLs.
[07:16] [07:30] Maya: ok jumping to procurement checklist — Anya, what's the internal gating items for vendor cert?
[07:36] Anya: primary items: legal signoff on MSA/DPA, security signoff on SOC2 + architecture, finance signoff on pricing, and vendor onboarding forms. After these we go to the board for final acceptance.
[07:48] Maya: understood. we'll aim to get the docs to you by end of the week.
[07:53] Diego: small question on network access — do you support static IP allow-listing for our egress?
[08:00] Liam: yes, for Dedicated and Private we provide static egress IPs. for Hosted we have shared pools but can provide a range request for enterprise customers at design time.
[08:13] Priya: any additional fees tied to static IPs or dedicated egress?
[08:18] Maya: there can be a small network egress surcharge for dedicated IP provisioning in certain cloud regions — we'll call it out in the pricing spreadsheet.
[08:30] Anya: will you accept a limited MSA amendment for indemnity in exchange for longer committed usage?
[08:38] Maya: possibly. commercial flex often comes with a trade — higher commit or larger ARR can move indemnity and warranty terms. we'll flag that as negotiable and include scenarios in the term sheet.
[08:50] [09:00] Priya: about billing cadence — monthly invoices ok? or do you require upfront for reserved capacity?
[09:07] Maya: reserved capacity typically billed monthly but requires a minimum term and can be prepaid for a discount. we'll show both cash and invoice credit scenarios.
[09:18] Diego: for incident transparency — do you provide a public incident timeline and post-mortems? we require vendor post-incident reports for severity 1s.
[09:27] Liam: yes, post-incident reports are standard. severity 1 gets an RCA within 72 hours for initial analysis and a full post-mortem in the following week. can include redacted traces as needed.
[09:40] Anya: ok good. are there any data residency exceptions we should watch for, like backups to a disaster recovery region?
[09:48] Liam: only if you select multi-region durability; we can turn that off. we'll put an explicit DPA option for "EU-only backups" vs "multi-region for DR" and list impacts on SLA and DR.
[10:05] [10:20] Maya: quick recap so we're aligned: we'll share the MSA redline tracker, a DPA with EU-only option and subprocessors list, a security packet (SOC2, diagrams), pricing spreadsheet with committed options and network surcharges, and an SLA appendix. any missing?
[10:36] Priya: benchmarks on caching impact if we do BYOK would be helpful.
[10:42] Liam: yes we'll run a short sample benchmark on your prompt set — we'll need sample prompts and typical session lengths.
[10:51] Anya: I'll upload a prompt set and sensitivity matrix to the shared folder after this call.
[11:00] Maya: perfect. next steps — schedule a legal deep-dive with your counsel and our legal lead. Anya, what times work next week?
[11:09] Anya: Tuesday afternoon or Thursday morning, we prefer Tuesday but will confirm.
[11:15] Priya: and finance follow-up — I'll review the pricing options and loop in our procurement approver by Friday.
[11:22] Maya: noted. any last-minute questions?
[11:25] Diego: curious about backup retention default — is it 90 days or longer?
[11:30] Liam: defaults vary by product, but 90 days is common; can be extended as a contract option.
[11:36] Anya: ok that's fine.
[11:40] Maya: great — thanks everyone. we'll send the packet and a commercial term sheet by Friday, set a follow-up for the legal deep-dive, and run the cache benchmark once we get prompts.
[11:53] Priya: thanks, appreciate it.
[12:00] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: some speaker labels were simplified by recorder; occasional words garbled (e.g., HSM vs HMS), timestamps are approximate. There was mild crosstalk during the SLA/pricing section.
